why_i_build: I build because I believe software should solve hard problems, not just exist. Every system I ship is designed to handle real-world edge cases — race conditions in financial transactions, latency in LLM inference, trust in anonymous marketplaces. Execution over theory.
principles: State is the source of truth — UI is a projection, not the data.
Latency is a feature — optimize for perceived speed, not just benchmarks.
Control the full stack — sovereignty over every layer eliminates black boxes.
Ship atomic units — every commit should be deployable and reversible.
Complexity is debt — if you can't explain it in one sentence, refactor it.
decision_style: I navigate trade-offs by anchoring to user impact. When choosing between architectural purity and shipping velocity, I ask: 'What breaks for the user if I defer this?' If the answer is 'nothing visible,' I ship now and refactor later. If the answer involves data integrity or trust, I engineer it correctly the first time, no exceptions.
